brief: DB's monthly dislocation note: rates markets have begun pricing a stress regime (wider sovereign spreads, higher yields) while equities and credit have not priced the consequences (lower growth, higher default risk), creating a bond-equity divergence DB expects to resolve toward risk assets, not persist indefinitely. Evidence: the Franco-German 10yr spread widened 32bps last week, the most since 1990, and the Italian spread over bunds widened 23bps, yet the STOXX 600 fell only 1.1% and Euro IG credit spreads rose only to 101bps, far below 2011-12/2020/2022 stress levels; the S&P 500 stayed within 1% of its record high. Separately, markets priced out Fed/ECB hikes on contagion fears, but DB argues above-target inflation limits how dovish central banks can turn, unlike the disinflationary 2010s. On oil, the futures curve has wrongly priced a Strait-of-Hormuz-driven decline for over six months while front-month Brent keeps grinding to fresh highs, and DB sees second-round inflation risk from the prolonged supply shock as understated. Unless financial stress eases quickly, as after SVB in 2023, DB expects risk assets to come under pressure, with a possible lag.

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: Euro investment-grade credit spreads rose only to 101 basis points by last Friday, far below levels seen during the 2011-12, 2020, and 2022 stress periods.
cards.anchor: Euro IG spreads have been remarkably calm, only rising to 101bps by Friday.

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: The S&P 500 closed within 1% of its record high last Friday even as global bond yields rose to multi-year highs.
cards.anchor: the S&P 500 closing within 1% of its record high last Friday

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: Deutsche Bank expects risk assets to come under mounting pressure unless the current financial stress eases quickly, as it did after SVB's collapse in March 2023.
cards.anchor: Unless the broader financial stress disappears quickly (as happened after SVB’s collapse in March 2023), then risk assets will come under mounting pressure.

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: Investors priced out the chance of further Fed and ECB rate hikes, including at the October decisions, after last week's contagion fears.
cards.anchor: investors priced out the chance of future rate hikes from the big central banks like the Fed and the ECB

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: Deutsche Bank argues that because inflation remains above target, central banks have inherently limited room to turn dovish in response to financial stress, unlike in the 2010s.
cards.anchor: because inflation is above target, there’s inherently a limit to how dovish central banks can become

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: In 2022-23, several episodes of financial stress produced dovish repricings of central bank rate paths that were each later unwound as above-target inflation reasserted itself.
cards.anchor: there were several moments of stress that led to a clear dovish repricing

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: The Brent oil futures curve is pricing a decline from a front-month price of $102 per barrel to $90 per barrel in six months and $83 per barrel in twelve months.
cards.anchor: the front-end Brent future is at $102/bbl, the 6-month future is at $90/bbl, the 12-month future is at $83/bbl.

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: The December 2026 Brent crude futures contract is hovering around its highest level to date, even as the futures curve continues to price a future price decline.
cards.anchor: the current front-end future for December 2026, which is now hovering around its highest levels to date

cards.document: What are the biggest market dislocations? October 2026
cards.claim: Brent crude oil prices fell significantly in June 2026 after an interim deal was agreed between the US and Iran, before the oil futures curve reverted to backwardation when the conflict re-escalated from July.
cards.anchor: oil prices fell significantly in June when the interim deal was agreed between the US and Iran

cards.anchor: Brent crude oil prices remain above $100/bbl, and broader commodity prices have risen significantly
